findings.summary: wall_color="#929292" is the same value as coil_edgecolor at :211, so the legend built at :283-289 draws 'coil sections' (1.4 pt) and 'first wall' (1.3 pt) as identical grey swatches; the two widths are not separable at the rendered 1400 px, so a reader cannot map either grey mark to a component. The contrast objective is met; what is lost is identification.

The first wall has no visible mark anywhere in the rendered PNG. draw_wall runs before draw_plasma_cells (:240 then :241) at a lower zorder and in the grey that :213 sets, and the cells are clipped to that same wall contour, so the purple cell outline covers the wall stroke along its whole length. Measured on the 1400x1074 render: all 8,362 mid-grey (#929292-range) pixels below the legend lie at x<=752 and belong to the coil rectangles and label antialiasing, with zero in the wall-detail panel at x>760, the panel whose subject is the wall. Positive control on the same mask: the same test detects the 'first wall' legend swatch (229 px at x 900-980, y<80), so the absence is not a broken instrument. The caption tells the reader the figure carries 'neutral coil and wall outlines', and the reader cannot find one.

item_verdicts.contrast: pass - label text is #333333 on white; the plasma-cell outline measures 4.58:1 median contrast against white in my own pixel measurement of this PNG, above the 3:1 the node targeted, and the two coil greys sit lighter than the mesh as intended.
item_verdicts.data_ink: pass - every mark is a stroke on white: unfilled coil rectangles, unfilled plasma cells and outlines, no filled regions. Measured ink (any channel below 90% white) is 6.72% of the canvas.
item_verdicts.decoration: pass - no gradient, background fill, shading, grid, axis, tick or frame; the only non-data marks are the 17 direct labels and a frameless three-entry legend above the panels.
item_verdicts.label_collision: pass - no label is clipped by the canvas and no label overlaps another or the plotted geometry: inspected at 3-5x on the rendered PNG over the legend band, the CS stack, both VS3 markers and the mesh edges, and no ink touches the outer three pixel rows or columns.
item_verdicts.legibility: pass - at 1400x1074 the reader gets the machine at a glance: coil sections are drawn as shapes and directly labelled (CS3U, CS2U, CS1 upper, CS1 lower, CS2L, CS3L, PF1-PF6, VS3 upper, VS3 lower), the 558-cell plasma mesh is the darkest and most detailed mark, and the right panel enlarges the same wall and mesh. The one reading gap is the first wall, which has no grey stroke of its own anywhere in the picture (see findings); its outline is readable only as the boundary the plasma cells are clipped to.
item_verdicts.table_form: pass - the image is poloidal geometry (coil sections, wall, cell mesh); none of the content is tabular.

justifications.contrast: Text is #333333; my pixel measurement of the plasma outline gives 4.58:1 median against white and the lightest mesh pixels stay above 3:1.
justifications.data_ink: 6.72% of the canvas carries ink by my own measurement; the white ground is the machine interior and the spacing the coil layout forces.
justifications.decoration: The render is pure line work with a frameless legend and no axes, ticks, grids, fills or gradients.
justifications.label_collision: Read the render at 3x and 5x over the legend, the CS stack, VS3 upper and VS3 lower: no collision, no clipping and no label over data; the outer pixel border is clean.
justifications.legibility: Coil identities are direct labels beside their shapes, so a reader never decodes a symbol table; the enlarged right panel makes the dense 558-cell mesh readable where the overview shows it at about 10 px per cell.
